claim: CAS relink-by-manifest has the same trust model as ordinary `ReplicatedMergeTree` interserver part fetch: the interserver channel is the trust boundary, and table-level RBAC is not a per-blob ACL.

The CAS stabilization iteration excludes large `CasGc.cpp` and `Cas::Store` structural refactors, new abstractions or configuration knobs without consumers, pre-emptive generality, and behavior changes justified only by taste.

The CAS fork uses three footprint rings: Ring 0 covers `ContentAddressed/` and `Core/`, Ring 1 covers CA-specific append-only lines in shared files, and Ring 2 covers shared upstream code that may be changed only when the delta shrinks, neutralizes, fixes, or simplifies the carried fork diff.

During `Store` teardown, a lease-renewal `on_lost` callback can re-arm `remount_thread` after its only join because `scheduleRemount` does not guard shutdown, causing an unjoined `ThreadFromGlobalPoolImpl` to terminate the process.
`Store::~Store` must latch a shutdown flag before joining `remount_thread`, `scheduleRemount` must refuse to spawn after that flag is set, and teardown must re-join after `mount_keeper->stop()`.
`MountLeaseKeeper` must join its renewal thread in `~MountLeaseKeeper()` before its `std::function` callbacks are destroyed.
`RunFileReader::next` trusts an un-checksummed `record_count` from the block head and can index beyond the block payload, violating `CasRunFile`'s fail-closed corruption contract.

A run-file block CRC must cover the block head, including `record_count`, `min_key`, and `max_key`, as well as the payload; `RunFileReader::next` must use bounds-checked decoding and require exact block consumption.

An uncaught `CORRUPTED_DATA` exception from `resolveByExactGet` or `putIfAbsentControlled` in `flushRefBatch` can leave `rt->leader_active` set and `rt->cv` unnotified, wedging the namespace's ref mutation path until restart.

When `flushRefBatch` catches a `CORRUPTED_DATA` exception, it must complete pending and carved survivor requests with that exception, reset `rt->leader_active`, notify `rt->cv`, keep the wedge on corruption, and rethrow.

The EDGE-BEFORE-OBSERVE invariant in `Build::observeAndAdmit` was guarded only by `chassert(precommitted)`, so release builds could adopt an existing incarnation without durable precommit and watermark protection.

`Build::observeAndAdmit` must throw `LOGICAL_ERROR` when the ADOPT path is reached with `precommitted == false`; fresh uploads before precommit remain legal because their watermark protection differs from adopted incarnations.
The non-Atomic part-path parser can anchor `data/<db>/<table>/detached/<part>/...` on the inner part-shaped component, producing a spurious table namespace that `DROP TABLE` never cleans.

For non-Atomic paths, `findPartDirComponent` must anchor on the first reserved `detached` component before scanning right-to-left for a part-shaped component, so detached paths fold into the table namespace with `part_name == detached`.

The CAS startup write/delete capability probe runs before the `skip_access_check` gate, so a mistyped bucket or transient DNS failure can prevent startup even when operators requested the start-now-fix-later path.
`PoolConfig::skip_access_check` skips `runCapabilityProbe` while keeping a CAS mount writable; owner, epoch, mount, and watermark bootstrap writes still occur.

The `skip_access_check` fix reads the per-disk configuration directive in the CA factory; global `skip_access_check` plumbing through shared `IDisk::startupImpl` and generic `DiskSelector` isolation remain deferred Ring-2 work.
`CasGcScheduler::runOneRoundNow` constructs a throwaway `Cas::Gc` and does not serialize with `loop`, so manual GC loses stable observer state and can run concurrently under one `gc_id`.

`CasGcScheduler` must share one persistent `Cas::Gc` between `loop` and `runOneRoundNow`, serialize rounds with a dedicated `gc_round_mutex`, and protect lazy `gc_scheduler` creation with `gc_scheduler_mutex`.
`CasGenerationSeal` decodes `RefNsCleanupState` and `TokenType` with unchecked `static_cast`, allowing invalid wire values to reach GC decision logic.
`decodeFoldSeal` must reject `TokenType` values outside `ETag`, `Generation`, and `Emulated`, and `RefNsCleanupState` values outside `Pending` and `Completed`, with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
`dropRefBestEffort` silently swallows rollback failures; a correlated backend outage can leave a permanently live phantom ref because GC reclaims only unreferenced objects.
Rollback failures swallowed by `dropRefBestEffort` must be logged with `tryLogCurrentException` and counted by `ProfileEvents::CasRefRollbackBestEffortDropFailed`.
The `suppress_destructive` decision for a GC round must be computed once in `Gc::fold`, stored in `FoldResult::suppress_destructive`, and reused by all destructive phases.
The CAS read path repeatedly parses the same raw part path for `existsFile`, `getFileSize`, `getStorageObjects`, and related metadata calls, causing repeated allocations per logical file-open.

Part-path classifiers use a thread-local MRU cache keyed only by the raw path because splitting is a pure, disk-agnostic operation; the cache is lock-free and reuses the split across `isPartFilePath` and `parsePartFilePath`.
The `getView` cache-hit path currently takes a per-disk `explain_mutex` and materializes `cacheKey()` repeatedly solely for a test/log-only decision journal.

`CachedPartFolderAccess::CacheParams::explain_enabled` defaults to `false`; when disabled, `recordDecision` takes neither the journal mutex nor a journal allocation, while `getView` computes one cache key and reuses it.

Process-global `CasGcIsLeader` and `CasGcPendingReclaimEntries` gauges are invalid with multiple CAS disks because their values are clobbered; per-disk health belongs on `system.content_addressed_mounts`.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` should expose per-disk `is_leader`, `pending_reclaim`, `last_success_age_seconds`, and `wedged_namespace_count` health columns.
`ProfileEvents::CasRefLatePredecessorObserved` counts each `trySnapshotPublishOnce` attempt whose `snapshot_min_log_age_ms` grace window stops at a young tail entry.
Object-storage token handling is consolidated into `tokenForHead`, `tokenForList`, and `tokenMatches` so native ETag, GCS generation, and emulated list-token policies have one source of truth.
CAS listing and exact-delete handling is intended to share a callback-based `forEachListedKey` iterator and a `classifyDeleteOutcome` classifier across GC, fsck, and orphan-manifest cleanup.
`Layout::blobKey`, `Layout::blobMetaKey`, and `Layout::parseBlobKey` are defined in a dedicated `CasLayout.cpp` because including `CasBlobRef.h` from `CasLayout.h` would create an include cycle.

Directory shape dispatch must preserve the fixed order `shadow → atomic-shard → table-uuid → part → subdir → generic`, and both `existsDirectory` and `listDirectory` must consume one shared routing table.
Borrowed projection storage shares the parent whole-part transaction: `DataPartStorageOnDiskFull::beginTransaction` and `commitTransaction` must be no-ops when `has_shared_transaction` is true.

The borrowed-projection transaction rule removes six duplicated `if (!isContentAddressed()) begin/commitTransaction()` guards from merge and mutate paths; the two sites that decide whether a projection borrows the parent transaction remain unchanged.

The pre-release CAS format cleanup removes the scalar `root_shards` from `PoolConfig`/`PoolMeta`, removes its proto field, and reserves proto field number 3 and name `root_shards`; the live `FoldResult::root_shards` vector is unrelated and must remain.

The `_precommits` namespace model and `isPrecommitNamespace` are dead because production ref keys use `_log/`, `_snap/`, and `_cleanup/`; their format modeling is removed without compatibility scaffolding.

`GcState::fence_seq` is write-only vestigial state because GC outcome and retire keys use `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)`; its proto field is removed and field number 3/name `fence_seq` are reserved.
`ShardCoverage::folded_cursor` and `ShardCoverage::incarnation` have no production readers and are removed from the fold-seal format while the `ShardIncarnation` type itself is retained.
The single-value `ObjectKind` enum is deliberately retained because it is threaded through about 100 consumers and removing it would be a refactor rather than clean subtraction.

The zero-increment `ProfileEvents` for removed shard mutation queues, pre-rebuild GC, manifest backpressure, and part-folder-view evictions, plus the unused `GcSnapPersist` event, are removed after confirming no increment sites or dashboard consumers.
`CasEvent::round` is not removed because it is a live serialized field surfaced as `system.content_addressed_log.round`, despite the earlier premise that it was always zero.
The stale `checkContentAddressedDiskRestrictions` no-op is removed from shared `MergeTreeData` because deleting it reduces the Ring-1 CA footprint rather than adding shared surface.

The wiring tests stop accepting legacy numeric ref-shard keys and classify current ref writes under `/cas/refs/` with `_log/` or `_snap/`; the two disabled tree-model tests remain deliberate documentation.

`SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` requires a distinct `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GC_REBUILD` privilege and an explicit disk; omitting the disk is a syntax error and naming a non-content-addressed disk is `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.

`registerContentAddressedMetadataStorage` must use the `gcs_max_conditional_put_bytes_` member name, throw `DB::Exception` with `NO_ELEMENTS_IN_CONFIG` when `server_root_id` is missing, and reconcile the `cas_` prefix on part-folder-cache keys.
`system.content_addressed_mounts.server_uuid` is typed as `UUID`, while `started_at_ms` and `expires_at_ms` are typed as `DateTime64(3)`.

The `ContentAddressedLog` system-log description must reflect that its configuration is enabled by default for the experimental CA feature; the stale `SystemLog.h` off-by-default wording is corrected.
The standalone `poc/cas_mergetree/` PoC is orphaned, superseded by `ContentAddressed/Core/`, referenced by nothing, and is deleted as repository hygiene.

The shared S3 412 policy is consolidated into `S3::isPreconditionFailedError` and `S3Exception::isPreconditionFailed`, checking the HTTP response code first and canonical exception name/message as fallback.

Before consolidation, `RetryStrategy` recognized HTTP 412 while `removeObjectIfTokenMatches` and `copyObjectConditional` used only exception name/message checks, missing stores such as RustFS that leave the exception name unparsed.

`Expect: 100-continue` negotiation is scoped to CAS-owned conditional writes using `WriteSettings::s3_conditional_write_use_expect_continue`, which defaults to `false`; non-CAS conditional writes such as Iceberg `If-None-Match` retain historical wire behavior.

The stabilization iteration defers the `CasGc.cpp` split, `Cas::Store` de-god-classing, generic `DiskSelector` per-disk isolation, `DiskObjectStorageTransaction` path virtualization, dead write-ordering code, and latent `MultipleDisksObjectStorageTransaction::shared_from_this` handling.

The TOKEN-implies-CONTENT startup probe is an open item because adding it to the backend contract has design value but may add surface; it is a candidate only if it can be implemented as a pure Ring-0 addition to the existing `Cas::Probe` battery.

Generic Ring-2 fixes such as `ThreadStatus` `parent_thread_group` retention, `ReadBufferFromFileView` position handling, `ReadBufferFromS3` cancel-stop, `LocalObjectStorage` TOCTOU robustness, `MergeTreeDeduplicationLog` null-writer fail-close, S3 conditional-write plumbing, GCS dialect/signer, and the 412/Expect fixes are tracked for separate upstream pull requests.

The work is sequenced as Phase 1 A1–A4 crash/corruption fixes, Phase 2 A5–A10 correctness fixes, Phase 3 D1–D5 removals, Phase 4 C1–C4 and Ring-2 shrinking, Phase 5 B1–B4 performance/operability, and Phase 6 C5 plus E1–E3 and F1; C5 lands last.
Concurrency tests for A1, A3, and A7 must avoid `sleep` and use deterministic fault injection, instrumented backends, or an atomic-gated second thread.
C5 is the only medium-risk behavioral change: it is a pure encapsulation of borrowed projection transactions, lands last with focused merge/mutate review, and can be reverted independently.

Removing `root_shards` and `fence_seq` is accepted because CAS is pre-release with no compatibility requirement; the affected pool-meta and GC-state codecs are covered by format tests and must have no remaining live consumers.

Changing run-file CRC coverage to include the block head changes the on-disk framing, which is acceptable pre-release because run files are attempt-scoped and short-lived; writer and reader must change together.
